Tests: apps/shuffler/test/port-tabletop/cardDiscardedEvent.test.ts and apps/shuffler/test/port-spine/cardDiscardedContract.test.ts, mirroring the card.played equivalents.), read the actual changed source files. Don't trust the description alone — verify what actually changed.

- **architecture.md**: Update if data flow, routes, rendering logic, or CSS structure changed.
- **history.md**: Add new entries for the changes just made. Include commit hashes if available.
- **interactions.md**: Update if new dependencies, dependents, or watch points were introduced. This is the most critical file — keep it accurate.
- **files.md**: Update if files were added, removed, or had their role change. Update line numbers if they shifted significantly.

content.content: 1 --- 2 name: two-faced-cards 3 kind: feature 4 --- 5 6 # Two-Faced Cards — a fleet-scoped feature owner 7 8 ## The Charge 9 10 **A card has faces; face is state, not identity.** 11 12 Identity is the Scryfall ID — it captures the exact printing, all faces, all names, 13 all image URIs. Which face is showing is *state* that travels with the card instance, 14 matters at play time (MDFCs are played as a chosen face), and is never part of the 15 card's identity. 16 17 **And face is two axes, not one** (decided 2026-08-07): **`face`** (`front`|`back` — which 18 *printed side* is chosen) is orthogonal to **face-down** (concealment — the identity is 19 hidden, and it looks like a card back or sleeve *even on a two-faced card*). A one-bit 20 "which side is up" model was proposed and rejected. So `face: "back"` is unreachable on a 21 one-faced card; a one-faced card turned over is **face-down**, not `face: back`. 22 23 **"Flip" does not mean the same thing on the two ships.** On the Shuffler, flip is 24 *inspection of a two-faced card* — a one-faced card cannot be flipped and shows no flip 25 affordance. On the Tabletop, *any* card can be turned over, because a card on a table is a 26 physical object with two sides; turning over a one-faced card puts it **face down**, which 27 is a real domain event. Full table in `CONTEXT-MAP.md`'s "Flip / Face-down" translation (root 28 of the repo); this owner's own copy of it lives in [tabletop.md](tabletop.md). 29 30 Every component of the fleet that touches cards must hold this: 31 32 - **Shuffler** — tracks `currentFace` on each GameCard, renders flip buttons, sends 33 the current face when a card leaves its boundary. The bulk of this knowledge base 34 (architecture, interactions, files, history) is Shuffler-component knowledge. 35 - **Tabletop** — renders the *played* face on arrival. **Ticket 12 landed 36 (2026-08-08)**: the card is now a genuine custom `mtg-card` tldraw shape (`BaseBoxShapeUtil`) 37 carrying `frontImageUrl`, `backImageUrl | null`, `face`, and `faceDown` in validated, 38 migratable `props`, and it renders its own `` — no per-instance tldraw image asset is 39 minted anymore. The arrival payload was unbaked to match: `card.played`'s scaffolding 40 `imageUrl` field is gone, replaced by `frontImageUrl` + `backImageUrl: string | null` 41 (`buildCardPlayedEvent` in `apps/shuffler/src/port-tabletop/types.ts`). **Physics ticket 06 42 resolved (2026-08-08)** the two questions that were open here: the trigger is two separate 43 context-menu items ("Flip" / "Turn face down"), and `currentFace` authority stays with the 44 Shuffler — flip-on-table is table-local, the divergence knowingly accepted. **Physics 45 ticket 17 built both gestures (2026-08-09, `eb24a4f`/`ff5d58a`)**: the Tabletop's first 46 custom tldraw `ContextMenu` (`CardContextMenu.tsx`) offers "Flip" (per-card `props.face` 47 swap, shown only when `backImageUrl !== null`) and "Turn face down"/"Turn face up" (a 48 convergent toggle of `props.faceDown` across the selection). A card entering the library 49 resets both axes to `face:'front', faceDown:false` in `MtgCardShapeUtil.onTranslateEnd`. 50 See [tabletop.md](tabletop.md). 51 - **Contract** — every event that *reveals or chooses* a face carries `face` beside 52 `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }` (`card.played`, and `card.discarded` once built — 53 a discard shows the card publicly). Events that remove a card from view carry **no** 54 face: `card.returned`, the `undo.*` kinds, and commanders riding `seat.joined` are all 55 faceless by decision (cards-come-and-go ticket 02, 2026-08-08 — Jess: "cards removed 56 from play no longer have a face up"). Names and image URLs are derivable 57 conveniences, not identity. See [contract.md](contract.md). 58 59 The sections below are the Shuffler-component view (the feature's birthplace). 60 61 ## Why This Feature Exists 62 63 Many Magic: The Gathering cards have two faces (transform, modal double-faced, reversible). In remote play via Mural/Discord, players need to see both sides of these cards. This feature flags such cards (`twoFaced`), shows a flip button backed by a flip animation, and tracks which face is currently showing. The back image is fetched from Scryfall on demand (same `scryfallId`, `face=back`) — no back-face data is stored. 64 65 ## Who Uses It and How 66 67 Players encounter two-faced cards throughout the app: 68 - **Prep page**: Flip the commander in place on the prepare screen, and flip any two-faced card in the card modal to inspect both sides. Flip state is not persisted here (yet) — both surfaces carry the face in the URL. 69 - **Game page**: Two-faced cards display with a flip button both inline (command zone, hand, etc.) and in the card modal. Flip state persists across page reloads. 70 - **Library search**: Multi-face cards appear in type groups for every face's/part's types, so a Creature//Planeswalker card shows up under both "Creature" and "Planeswalker." This is driven by `CardDefinition.cardTypes` (the union of all faces' types), not by a flip flag. 71 72 ## Design Philosophy 73 74 - **Flip is a UI concern, not a game event.** The app tracks where cards are (Library, Hand, Table, etc.) but doesn't model battlefield state. Flipping doesn't change where a card is, so it's not recorded in the event log. 1 # Two-Faced Cards Architecture 2 3 ## Data Model 4 5 ### CardDefinition (`src/types.ts`) 6 Every card has: 7 - `twoFaced: boolean` — whether the card has a separate back image (drives the flip button) 8 - `cardTypes: string[]` — the union of every face's/part's types (e.g. `["Legendary","Creature","Planeswalker"]`) 9 10 Plus identity fields: `name`, `scryfallId`, `multiverseid?`, `oracleCardName`, `colorIdentity`, `set`. There is **no** `CardFace`/`backFace` and no `manaCost`/`cmc`/`oracleText` — those were removed (commit `f76b49c`) since the card is displayed as a Scryfall image and nothing read them. The flip button needs only `twoFaced` + `scryfallId`; library grouping needs only `cardTypes`. 11 12 ### GameCard (`src/port-persist-state/types.ts:72-78`) 13 Runtime game state tracks: 14 - `currentFace: "front" | "back"` — which face is currently showing 15 16 ### PersistedGameCard (`src/port-persist-state/persisted-types.ts:24-30`) 17 Persisted version also stores `currentFace`. On hydration, the full `CardDefinition` is loaded from the card repository, and `currentFace` comes from the persisted game card. 18 19 ## What Counts as Two-Faced (layout allowlist) 20 21 **`twoFaced` means "two separate physical faces, each with its own image" — NOT "two entries in the source data's faces array."** Many single-image layouts (split, adventure, aftermath, flip, and Strixhaven's `prepare`) print both halves on one front face. They have two `faces` in the data but no back image, so a flip button would request a nonexistent Scryfall `face=back` image. 22 23 The single source of truth is `src/port-deck-retrieval/twoFacedLayouts.ts`: 24 - `DOUBLE_SIDED_LAYOUTS = ["transform", "modal_dfc", "reversible_card", "double_faced_token"]` 25 - `isDoubleSidedLayout(layout)` — true only for those layouts 26 27 Both adapters use it, so they agree on what's flippable. 28 29 ## Data Flow: Ingestion 30 31 ### Archidekt Adapter (`src/port-deck-retrieval/archidektAdapter/ArchidektDeckToDeckAdapter.ts:84-110`) 32 - `multiFace = faces.length === 2` — card has two faces in the data (any layout) 33 - `twoFaced = multiFace && isDoubleSidedLayout(layout)` — only genuinely double-sided layouts 34 - `cardTypes = multiFace ? union(faces[].types) : oracleCard.types` — every face's types, deduped. (Top-level types for split-layout cards are unreliable, so use the per-face arrays.) 35 - Reads `layout` from `archidektCard.card.oracleCard.layout` (`layout?: string` in `archidektTypes.ts`) 36 37 ### MTGJSON Adapter (`src/port-deck-retrieval/mtgjsonAdapter/MtgjsonDeckAdapter.ts:66-100`) 38 - `twoFaced = isDoubleSidedLayout(mtgjsonCard.layout)` (shared with Archidekt) 39 - `cardTypes = union(card.types + every otherFaceIds face's types)`, resolved from `cardsByUuid`, **regardless of layout** — this captures the second part of adventure/split cards (e.g. `Eiganjo Dynastorian // Replenish` → `[Creature, Sorcery]`). 40 - Throws if a genuine double-sided card's other face can't be resolved (AllIdentifiers missing) — message "no other face found". 41 42 ### Card Repository Storage (`src/port-card-repository/SqliteCardRepositoryAdapter.ts`) 43 - `card_types` column stores JSON-serialized `string[]`; `two_faced` stores 0/1 44 - `image_uris` / `back_image_uris` columns store JSON-serialized `CardImageUris` (nullable). Added via non-destructive `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (existing rows get NULL → fallback to constructed URLs). 45 - No `back_face`/`mana_cost`/`cmc`/`oracle_text` columns. The table is a gitignored cache; on startup an old-schema table (one lacking `card_types`) is DROPped and recreated. 46 47 ## Data Flow: Flip in Game 48 49 ``` 50 User clicks "Flip" button 51 → POST /flip-card/:gameId/:gameCardIndex (inline flip) 52 → POST /flip-card-modal/:gameId/:gameCardIndex (modal flip) 53 → loadGameFromParams middleware loads GameState 54 → requireValidVersion middleware checks optimistic lock 55 → GameState.flipCard(gameCardIndex) toggles currentFace 56 → persistStatePort.save() persists new face state 57 → Response: updated HTML fragment 58 - inline: formatFlippingContainer() (just the flip container) 59 - modal: full card-modal partial (with image, actions, navigation) 60 → HX-Trigger: "game-state-updated" refreshes game container 61 ``` 62 63 ### Inline Flip (`/flip-card/`) 64 - Returns the `formatFlippingContainer()` HTML, which replaces the `#card-N-outer-flip-container-with-button` element 65 - The flip button uses `hx-swap="outerHTML"` and `hx-target` pointing at its own container 66 - Uses `onclick="event.stopPropagation()"` to prevent the card click (which opens the modal) from firing 67 68 ### Modal Flip (`/flip-card-modal/`) 69 - Returns the full card modal partial, replacing `#card-modal-container` contents 70 - Preserves navigation context: reads `navList` from request body and passes it through to the new flip button and nav arrows 71 - This was a hard-won design — earlier attempts tried to flip within the modal without a full re-render, which caused the modal to close 72 73 ## Data Flow: Flip on Prep Page 74 75 There are two prep flip surfaces, both stateless: 76 77 ``` 78 User clicks "Flip" in prep card modal 79 → GET /prep-card-modal/:prepId/:cardIndex?face=back(&navList=...) 80 → Reads prep from persistence 81 → Uses ?face query param to determine which face to show 82 → Constructs image URL with face parameter 83 → Flip button links back with opposite face value 84 → No state mutation — purely URL-driven 85 ``` 86 87 ``` 88 User clicks "Flip" under the commander on the prepare screen (inline) 89 → GET /prep-flip-card/:prepId/:cardIndex?face=back 90 → Reads prep from persistence (404 if absent) 91 → Finds the card via createPrepViewHelpers — same commanders-then-library-cards 92 indexing as /prep-card-modal (404 unknown index, 400 single-faced) 93 → Response: renderCommanderCard() — the WHOLE card container for that face 94 → hx-swap="outerHTML" onto #card-N-container 95 → No state mutation, nothing persisted 96 ``` 97 98 **Why prep swaps the whole container and game swaps only the flip container.** The 99 container carries the card-modal URL. In a game that URL needs no face — the modal route 100 reads `currentFace` off the game — so only the inner flip container is replaced. On the 101 prepare screen the face is *page state*, so the container's URL carries `?face=` and must 102 be re-rendered on every flip to stay truthful. Hence two different `hx-target`s from the 103 same function, chosen by `FlipRequest.page`. 104 105 **The rejected alternative, worth not re-deriving:** put `hx-vals='js:{face: …classList.contains("card-flipped") …}'` 106 on the container to read the face at click time. It fails. `hx-vals` is inherited by 107 descendants, the flip button is a descendant, and htmx appends GET params to an existing 108 query string (`R.indexOf("?") < 0 ? "?" : "&"`), so the button would request 109 `?face=back&face=front`. Express reads a repeated key as an **array**, so 110 `req.query.face === "back"` is false and the route silently serves the front face — 111 breaking Flip in the same invisible way as the original JES-90 bug. 112 113 Key difference from game flip: prep flip is stateless. The face is a query parameter, not persisted. On a page reload the card shows the front face again. 114 115 The two prep surfaces are deliberately one-way: the page tells the modal which face to open on (via `?face=` in the container's modal URL), but flipping *inside* the modal changes only the modal. That's intended — the modal is its own view of the card, not a controller for the page. 116 117 **Never point a prep surface at a game flip route.** `prepId` and `gameId` come from independent SQLite sequences (`game_preps` vs `game_states`), so a prepId handed to `/flip-card/:gameId/...` either finds no game or finds an unrelated one — and `validateStateVersion` allows a missing `expected-version`, so the unrelated game would be mutated and saved. This was the JES-90 bug. 118 119 ## View Rendering 120 121 ### `formatCardContainer()` (`src/view/common/shared-components.ts`) 122 Branches on `gameCard.card.twoFaced`: 123 - **Two-faced**: wraps card in `formatFlippingContainer()` with flip animation structure 124 - **Single-faced**: simple `` tag 125 126 Takes an optional `flipRequest?: FlipRequest` that says how the flip button should ask for the other face. It defaults to `{ page: "game", gameId, expectedVersion }`, so game call sites pass nothing and get the POST behavior; the prepare screen passes `{ page: "prep", prepId }`. 127 128 ### `FlipRequest` (`src/view/common/shared-components.ts`) 129 ```typescript 130 type FlipRequest = 131 | { page: "game"; gameId: number; expectedVersion?: number } // POST, mutates state 132 | { page: "prep"; prepId: number }; // GET ?face=, stateless 133 ``` 134 This exists so the page asking for the flip is explicit rather than inferred from a numeric id — the two id spaces are not interchangeable (see the prep flip data flow above). 135 136 ### `formatFlippingContainer()` (`src/view/common/shared-components.ts`) 137 Signature is `(gameCard: GameCard, flipRequest: FlipRequest)`. Builds the 3D CSS flip structure: 138 ``` 139 div.flip-container-with-button 140 div.flip-container-outer [.card-flipped if back face showing] 141 div.flip-container-inner 142 img.two-sided-back (back face image) 143 img.two-sided-front (front face image) 144 button.flip-button (per flipRequest: POST /flip-card/ in game, GET /prep-flip-card/?face= in prep) 145 ``` 146 Both face images are always in the DOM. CSS 3D transforms with `backface-visibility: hidden` show only the current face. The `.card-flipped` class triggers a 180-degree Y rotation. 147 148 ### Image URLs (`src/types.ts`) 149 Two functions now exist: 150 - **`getCardImageUrl(card: CardDefinition, format, face)`** — the one views call. Prefers the **stored** Scryfall URL on the card (`card.imageUris` for front, `card.backImageUris` for back), falling back to construction when absent. 151 - **`constructCardImageUrl(scryfallId, format, face)`** — the old by-hand construction (`https://cards.scryfall.io/{format}/{face}/{id[0]}/{id[1]}/{scryfallId}.{ext}`), kept as the fallback. The `face` (`"front"`/`"back"`) is part of the path. 152 153 **Why stored URLs:** the bare constructed `normal` URL 404s for very recently released cards (e.g. Arcane Signet, set ECC) — Scryfall only serves them at the **versioned** URL (`...jpg?`). The stored URLs are copied verbatim from Scryfall (so they carry the `?` tag). 154 155 `CardDefinition` carries two **optional** fields for this: `imageUris?: CardImageUris` (front/only face) and `backImageUris?: CardImageUris` (present only when `twoFaced`). `CardImageUris = Partial>`, storing only the formats the app uses (`normal`, `large`, `png`, `art_crop`). Both faces still share **one** `scryfallId`; the back is no longer derived by path-swapping the same id at render — it comes from `card_faces[1].image_uris` at ingestion. The fields are optional with a graceful fallback, so legacy data (no stored URLs) still renders via construction. 156 157 ### Image enrichment at ingestion (`src/port-card-images/`) 158 A new port fetches Scryfall image URLs by scryfallId: 159 - `CardImagesPort` / `FetchedCardImages` (`{front, back?}`) — `types.ts` 160 - `ScryfallCardImagesGateway` — batches `POST https://api.scryfall.com/cards/collection` (75 ids/request, caches across calls, sends `User-Agent`+`Accept` headers Scryfall requires). Pure mapper `mapScryfallCardToImages`: single-faced reads top-level `image_uris`; genuine DFCs read `card_faces[0].image_uris` (front) and `card_faces[1].image_uris` (back). 161 - `FakeCardImagesGateway` — test fake (synthesizes deterministic versioned URLs, or seed specific ids). 162 - `enrichDeckWithImages(deck, port)` — collects unique scryfallIds, fetches, attaches `imageUris` to every card and `backImageUris` only to `twoFaced` cards. Best-effort: cards Scryfall doesn't return are left unset → fallback. 163 164 Enrichment runs: Archidekt adapter (optional injected `imagesPort`, wired in `server.ts` + `download-deck` script), and the `fetch-mtgjson-precons` script after conversion. The MTGJSON adapter's `convertMtgjsonToDeck` stays synchronous (enrichment is a separate post-pass). 165 166 ## CSS Animation 167 168 Two separate CSS files define flip styles: 169 170 ### `public/game.css` (lines 104-143) 171 - Card dimensions: 200px × 278px 172 - `perspective: 1000px` on outer container 173 - `transition: transform 0.8s` on inner container 174 - `transform: rotateY(180deg)` when `.card-flipped` 175 - `translateX(-100px)` offset for centering 176 177 ### `public/prepare.css` (lines 221-276) 178 - Same flip mechanics but with prep-page-specific styling 179 - Additional `.flip-button` styling (positioned below card) 180 - `.flip-container-with-button` layout container 181 182 ### `public/playmat.css` (line 463) 183 - `.modal-action-button.flip-button` — styles the flip button inside the card modal 184 185 ## How to Tell Which Face Is Showing (observables for tests) 186 187 Face state is observable in the DOM, differently on each surface. 188 189 **Inline (game and prep pages)** — the strong one: 190 - `.flip-container-outer` gains the class **`.card-flipped`** when `currentFace === "back"` 191 (`formatFlippingContainer`, `shared-components.ts:104`). Assert on the class, not the 192 animation — the 0.8s transition is the animations owner's territory and `.card-flipped` 193 is applied server-side, present the instant the swap settles. 194 - Both face images are always in the DOM (`.two-sided-front` / `.two-sided-back`), so image 195 presence proves nothing; only the class distinguishes. 196 197 **Card modal (game and prep)** — the strong observable here too: 198 - **`.card-modal-overlay` carries `data-current-face="<%= currentFace %>"`** (added to 199 `views/partials/card-modal.ejs`; `currentFace` was already passed into the template, just 200 never rendered). Assert `data-current-face` equals `"front"`/`"back"` — this works 201 identically on both the game and prep modals, closing the gap where the game modal 202 previously had no reliable face observable. `verify-library-grouping.spec.ts` uses this. 203 - The older indirect observables still work and remain useful when the attribute isn't 204 convenient to check: 205 - **`img.modal-card-image`'s `src`** — `getCardImageUrl(card, "large", currentFace)`, so it 206 differs between faces on both pages. With stored URLs the two faces are different Scryfall 207 files (`card_faces[0]` vs `[1]`); with the constructed fallback the path segment is 208 `/large/front/` vs `/large/back/`. Same URL also appears in the Copy button's `onclick`. 209 - **Prep only: the flip button's own `hx-get`** carries the *target* face — 210 `/prep-card-modal/:prepId/:i?face=` (`app.ts:945-951`). Showing the front ⇒ the 211 button reads `?face=back`, and vice versa. The **game** flip button is a `hx-post` to a 212 toggling route, byte-identical on both faces, so it was never usable as an observable — 213 `data-current-face` is the fix for that gap specifically. 214 215 ## Type Merging for Library Search 216 217 In both game and prep library modal routes (`src/app.ts`), when mapping cards for the library search template: 218 ```typescript 219 cardTypes: gc.card.cardTypes 220 ``` 221 `cardTypes` is already the deduplicated union of all faces' types (computed at ingestion), so a transform card appears in all relevant type groups with no per-request merge.
